_doc: Renderings for the translator. `es` = the term to use; `note` = which context or how; `avoid` = a less suitable house choice here (not always wrong Spanish). Inflect freely. v2 2026-11-20 after Codex's review of the pack.

terms.en: reading (Evelyn interpreting the cards the buyer chose)
terms.note: *tu tirada*, *lo que dicen tus cartas*. ONLY on /fb-tarot pages and in card reads. Pages both funnels share (chat, order bump, checkout, upsells, success page) may be seen by a buyer who never saw a card: there it is *consulta*
*nuestra consulta*, *durante esta consulta*

terms.en: reading (the written 5–7 page deliverable sent by email)
terms.es: tu lectura / tu lectura por escrito
terms.note: the same noun everywhere (chat, checkout, success page, emails). Add *personalizada* only where the English says personalized or personal; never add it as a product claim the line doesn't make

terms.en: double reading / Double Your Reading (order bump)
terms.es: una segunda lectura (on the second topic)
terms.note: the bump is a second written reading on a second topic ({topic}): say that, e.g. *una segunda lectura, sobre tu {topic}*. Never add a claim the line doesn't make (more depth, more detail, twice as far)
avoid: doble lectura (ambiguous: it can mean a double meaning)

terms.note: lower case in running text; as a title or button, capital on the first word only

*limpiar tu energía*, *liberarte de ese peso*. *Una limpia* (the everyday Mexican word for a spiritual cleansing) only where the English names an actual cleansing, never for any release or letting go; never add how one is done (egg, herbs, copal)

terms.es: bloqueo / lo que te frena / los obstáculos (by meaning)
terms.note: *tener los caminos cerrados* / *abrir caminos* only where the English already describes a spiritual obstruction; for an ordinary difficulty use *lo que te frena*
*piedra volcánica* is the usual word in Mexico
say with what on first mention; *cargada* alone can read as heavy or loaded
the product name; say on first mention what it is for
avoid: brazalete (a less suitable house choice for a beaded stone bracelet)

terms.note: *manifestar* is normal in Spanish law-of-attraction speech; *atraer* where it reads more natural
*salvia blanca* when the English says white sage

avoid: agua bendita for water Evelyn blessed
terms.note: say who blessed it where it matters; keep *agua bendita* only where the English means church holy water
*una vidente*; her ability is *su don* (*tu don* for the buyer's)
avoid: regalo for a gift that means an ability

terms.note: never mix them: *tus cartas* on the table, *tu tarjeta* at checkout

*correo electrónico* on the form field and wherever delivery is first explained, confirmed or missing (plain *correo* can mean postal mail, and the funnel also ships physical items); *correo* only once the channel is clear
STOP and HELP stay in English as the commands to type (*Responde STOP para cancelar*); never claim they are the only way to stop

terms.es: Línea 988 de Prevención del Suicidio y Crisis
terms.note: the Spanish service: *llama al 988 y marca 2 para español, o envía AYUDA por mensaje de texto al 988* (988lifeline.org/es, checked 2026-11-20)
Crisis Text Line's Spanish keyword is AYUDA, not a translation of HOME (crisistextline.org/es, checked 2026-11-20)
*te devolvemos tu dinero* where a verb reads better

tarot._doc: Spanish tarot names for the Rider-Waite cards shown. House choice: Oros and Sota (the names most Mexican readers know); Pentáculos and Paje are valid alternatives, never corrected as errors. Card names are proper names, capitalized as below even in running text, but the article is lower case and contracts there: *te salió el Mago*, *la carta del Mago*. Minor cards: *el Dos de Oros*, *la Sota de Copas*, *el As de Espadas*. Reversed: *invertida* / *invertido*, agreeing with the card: *la Sota de Oros invertida*, *el Colgado invertido*.
